title: Running on Empty, Quietly
summary: Two colleagues talk about the early signs that a pace is not working, small protections that help, and where support lives for state employees.
learningObjective: Two colleagues talk about the early signs that a pace is not working, small protections that help, and where support lives for state employees.

sources.title: U.S. Office of the Surgeon General — Framework for Workplace Mental Health and Well-Being
WHO: Burnout as an occupational phenomenon
MMB: Lifestyle Benefits and counseling FAQ

turns.speaker: host1
turns.chapter: Good at it and running down
turns.text: Here's someone a lot of us know. A case manager, two years with a full caseload, and really good at it. Lately they answer email at ten at night, skip lunch and feel flat even after a good outcome for a family.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.chapter: Good at it and running down
turns.text: Nothing's on fire. The work is getting done. So is there actually a problem?

turns.speaker: host1
turns.chapter: Good at it and running down
turns.text: That's the trap. The early signs are quiet. Feeling flat after a win is one of them. The World Health Organization describes burnout as a result of workplace stress that hasn't been managed: exhaustion, growing distance from the work and feeling less effective.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.chapter: Good at it and running down
turns.text: So it's about the conditions at work, not a personal failing.

turns.speaker: host1
turns.chapter: Good at it and running down
turns.text: Right. And that matters, because it means some of the fixes are things a team can change together.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.text: Okay, practical moment. It's 9:45 at night. A colleague emails a non-urgent question about next week's schedule. I'm going to answer it. It takes thirty seconds.

turns.speaker: host1
turns.text: It does. And it also tells your colleague that late-night answers are normal here. Next week, they'll feel they should answer at ten, too.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.text: Huh. So the thirty seconds isn't really the cost.

turns.speaker: host1
turns.text: No. One small protection is to schedule the reply for the morning, or simply answer it at nine. The question still gets answered. The norm doesn't spread.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.text: What about when it's more than email? Caseload up by a third since spring, two reports late, and I haven't said anything to my supervisor.

turns.speaker: host1
turns.text: That's the moment to raise it, while it's two reports and not ten. Bring facts and a question: here's what's changed, here's what's slipping, which of these should I put first?

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.text: That's much easier to say than, I'm not coping.

turns.speaker: host1
turns.text: And it's more useful to a supervisor. They can actually decide something.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.chapter: Noticing a colleague, and where support lives
turns.text: Last one. A colleague has seemed withdrawn for a few weeks and left early twice without saying goodbye. I don't want to pry.

turns.speaker: host1
turns.chapter: Noticing a colleague, and where support lives
turns.text: You don't have to diagnose anything. A private, simple check-in works: I've noticed you seem a bit quieter lately. How are you doing? Then listen, and let them decide how much to share.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.chapter: Noticing a colleague, and where support lives

turns.speaker: host1
turns.chapter: Noticing a colleague, and where support lives
turns.text: Know where support lives. Minnesota's state Employee Assistance Program is free, voluntary and confidential, for state employees and the people they live with. And if someone may be in crisis, the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline answers by call, text or chat, any time.

turns.speaker: geffen
turns.chapter: Noticing a colleague, and where support lives
turns.text: So the course isn't about fixing anyone. It's about noticing early, and knowing the next step.
